message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that requires careful planning, safety precautions, and specialized equipment. While the exact duration can vary depending on weather, crew size, and logistical factors, here’s a general breakdown:

| Step | Typical Duration (per crew) |
|------|-----------------------------|
| **Preparation & Safety Setup** | 1–2 weeks (setting up scaffolding, safety barriers, permits) |
| **Cleaning & Surface Prep** | 1–2 weeks (pressure washing, rust removal, priming) |
| **Primer Application** | 1 week (multiple passes, drying time between coats) |
| **Base Coat & Color Layers** | 2–3 weeks (each coat may require 24–48 h drying time) |
| **Final Coats & Touch‑ups** | 1–2 weeks (inspection, corrections, protective clear coat) |

**Total Estimated Time:** Roughly **6–10 weeks** of active work, though this is often spread out over several months because crews work in shifts, weather delays can occur, and safety inspections add extra time.

For context, the Eiffel Tower is repainted roughly every 7 years. Each full repaint cycle typically involves a team of 30–40 skilled painters working in shifts, covering about 5,000 square meters of surface area. The process is carefully scheduled to minimize disruption to visitors and maintain structural integrity.

So, while the physical act of painting each section might only take a few days per crew, the overall project usually spans **two to three months** from start to finish.
